To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) sneutrino exchange can be identified with a significance of 3.2 σ (2.2 σ ) for a center-of-mass energy of 1 TeV (500 GeV), assuming a total integrated luminosity of 500 fb − 1 and 80% beam polarization, and (b) the identification of the sneutrino is more efficient for the electron channel than for the muon channel

(i) the sneutrino exchange scenario can be identified in the double polarization asymmetry with a high degree of confidence; (ii) the identification can be performed in a wide range of sneutrino mass values, from 100 GeV to 1 TeV.

the identification reach for the sneutrino exchange is 2.3 TeV for 500 fb −1 of integrated luminosity, and 3 TeV for an integrated luminosity of 1000 fb −1, assuming a center-of-mass energy of 1 TeV and 90% polarization for both beams.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of the possibility of uniquely distinguishing sneutrino exchange against other non-standard interactions in lepton pair productions at ILC with both beams being polarised.
the identification of the indirect effects of sneutrino exchange against other possible sources of new physics in the lepton pair production process.
the possibility of identifying the indirect effects in lepton pair events of sneutrino exchange at the ILC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
sneutrino exchange can be identified in a large fraction of the parameter space of the R -parity violating supersymmetry, and in a large fraction, too, of the parameter space for the other models.
the ILC can identify the indirect effects of sneutrino exchange with a significance level of 5 σ for a center-of-mass energy of 1 T eV and an integrated luminosity of 500 f b − 1.
sneutrino exchange can be identified in lepton pair final states at ILC with a high confidence, if the sneutrino mass is below the beam energy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sneutrino exchange can be identified in lepton pair productions at the ILC with polarised beams, and the identification reach on it is about 2 TeV.
the sneutrino effects can be distinguished from all other competitive scenarios at ILC with a luminosity of about 500 fb −1, if the beams are polarized with a maximum degree.
the ILC with its full set of polarized beams is an optimal tool to identify the origin of the new physics scenario.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sneutrino exchange can be uniquely identified in the case of a large deviation of the asymmetry from the SM expectation, even when the deviation is as small as 1% of the cross section.
the sneutrino effects are clearly distinguishable from the others, with a statistical significance of at least 5 σ for a large range of center-of-mass energies.
the identification of sneutrino exchange can be achieved at the 5 σ level for sneutrino masses as high as 1.5 TeV.
